Despite the expansion of GNN models aiming to capture richer representations of graph-structured data, the deep variants often encounter the issue of \u0022feature-smoothing.\u0022 This phenomenon inhibits their performance potential, limiting their ability to extract and preserve meaningful information from graph inputs. To tackle this challenge, I propose the Hierarchical Line Graph Neural Network (HLGNN), a novel framework that leverages the concept of iterated line graphs from graph theory. While line graph transformation\u2014a method for converting a graph into its line graph representation to capture higher-order connectivity patterns\u2014has gained attention in graph theory, its application within the realm of graph neural networks remains under-explored. Inspired by the principles of hierarchical and higher-order GNNs, I introduce a message-passing mechanism within HLGNN that facilitates the flow of information across both intra-graph and inter-graph levels. This hierarchical approach enables HLGNN to address the feature-smoothing problem effectively while enhancing the model\u0027s capacity to capture complex graph structures. The versatility of HLGNN extends to various graph-related tasks, including node classification, graph classification, and community detection.
